item.title: Beloved football broadcaster Danny Kelly dies aged 69
item.description: The popular sports broadcaster Danny Kelly has died aged 69 after a battle with cancer. A lifelong Tottenham fan, but beloved by fans from all clubs, Kelly announced earlier this year that he had been diagnosed with oesophageal cancer. Kelly featured on popular shows Kick Off, Sporting Life and Trans-Euro Express, while also featuring on The Athletic’s Tottenham podcast The View From The Lane. Kelly was also a music lover and spent two years as editor of the NME. And the football community is mourning the loss of the beloved presenter, with talkSPORT paying tribute to Kelly and sharing one of his most iconic quotes on air: “I love football, Stan. I love it.” The broadcaster added that Kelly was “a cherished part of talkSPORT for so many years” and brought “extraordinary wit, warmth and knowledge to our airwaves. His passion for football, music and life was infectious, and his kindness touched everyone around him.” Friend and fellow broadcaster Danny Baker said: “My great friend, supreme broadcaster and funniest man I ever knew, Danny Kelly, died yesterday afternoon. I cannot believe I will never hear his voice again.” talkSPORT colleague Ian ‘Moose’ Abrahams said: “Absolutely heartbroken to hear Danny Kelly has passed away. One of the best broadcasters I’ve worked with. One of the most amazing, kindest, funny, passionate people I knew. Danny, we’ll always have “I love Football”. I will miss you my friend, sleep well.” Former Crystal Palace owner and talkSPORT pundit Simon Jordan said: "He was a brilliant broadcaster, editor, writer and friend, the reason I'm able to broadcast is because of Danny, it started with Danny, he nurtured me. He was an ideas factory. He fought this battle, the adversity he went through, the sadness, I feel choked, we thought Danny was coming through. He showed such strength and courage. “We had such fun, during Covid we had such little material, nothing was going on, we had ideological debates, we disagreed, but we still created a dynamic between us, it’s stayed with me. I know him from years back. He will be missed, by those who knew him, the way he’d tell stories, strong views.” More follows...

item.title: “They Just Annoyed Each Other” – Mets Insider Offers Fresh Perspective on Francisco Lindor and Juan Soto’s Clubhouse Dynamic
item.description: Francisco Lindor and Juan Soto - NY Mets © Imagn Mets insider Chelsea Janes offered a fresh perspective on the relationship between team superstars Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor. Although multiple reports during the regular season suggested a potential fallout or rift between the two, Janes said their relationship had been rocky but not exactly destructive. Furthermore, she said that toward the end of the season, Soto went out of his way to show a stronger on-field relationship with Lindor. The Puerto Rican had once called Soto “my brother” and publicly dismissed rumors of a rift. Janes made the remarks during her appearance on ‘Foul Territory.’ “Soto and Lindor, yeah, they both, from what I could see and from what I heard, made a lot of effort this year to just put a better public face on a relationship that I think was rocky, but rocky in a way that doesn’t have to be destructive. I think they just annoyed each other. I think it’s kind of that simple,” Janes said. “I don’t think it’s that deep. And late in the year, I think Soto especially went out of his way to make sure you saw him giving Lindor high fives, and you see them chatting. I think Lindor said, Look, I’ve learned a lot. You can’t come in hot in relationships. You have friendships. You got to let things develop over time,” she added. Watch the video here: Rumors of a chilly dynamic and early tension emerged after Soto signed his massive 15-year, $765 million contract during the 2024 offseason. In June, former Mets starting pitcher Freddy Peralta reportedly helped facilitate a conversation between the two to clear the air. Despite their differing personalities, both players have repeatedly and publicly rejected speculation of a fallout, dismissing drama fueled by baseless media reports. MLB.com Mets beat writer Anthony DiComo did so in July, downplaying any friction between the two. MLB Insider Terms Juan Soto-Francisco Lindor Friction as “Overblown” In his July article for MLB.com , DiComo noted that the Soto-Lindor friction had been blown out of proportion. He added that both players had told The Athletic their relationship was fine, a claim backed by multiple Mets insiders and analysts. DiComo concluded that both players believed they could make the team better together. “Reports of friction between the two Mets stars appear overblown. Both players recently told The Athletic that their relationship is fine, and multiple Mets insiders have corroborated that viewpoint. Whether the two got along last year isn’t relevant to the current situation. Personalities aside, both Soto and Lindor recognize that they can form a better team together,” DiComo wrote. Despite two stars on its roster, New York missed the playoffs for a second straight season and finished last in the NL East for the first time in 23 years. item.title: Kirk Cousins sends short and sweet message to Minnesota Vikings after trade
item.description: Photo by Cindy Ord/Getty Images for SiriusXM Kirk Cousins is returning to the team with whom he enjoyed his best NFL years, and he has shared his excitement in just five words. The answer that the Minnesota Vikings have found for their quarterback issues is none other than Kirk Cousins. Between 2018 and 2023, he was the franchise quarterback, earning three Pro Bowl selections during that time. He moved on eventually, signing a big contract with the Atlanta Falcons. However, Cousins is now back with the NFC North franchise. The quarterback was acquired in a trade from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a 2027 third-round draft pick. There is naturally a lot of attention being paid to this story, but the QB himself has kept it simple. Kirk Cousins tells Minnesota he will ‘see them soon’ after trade announcement The team feels like they are simply one decent quarterback away from being considered serious Super Bowl contenders. And while Cousins may be on the older side now, he is certainly a good QB. And as long as he passes the medical test, he will be the man to lead the Vikings once again. The 38-year-old knows the situation he is walking into, and based on the message he shared on his Instagram , he is more than happy to let his game do the talking rather than just words. “See you soon, MN! #Skol,” was all the quarterback said in his caption, sharing a picture of him running out in a Vikings uniform. ‘Skol’, of course, is part of the fan chant and the fight song for the franchise, which means Cousins is showcasing his knowledge of the team. Cousins has put together a solid statistical season so far, throwing for 2,340 yards and 20 touchdowns against eight interceptions in nine games for the Las Vegas Raiders. He is completing 64.1 percent of his passes with a 97.1 passer rating. He might just be the answer for the Vikings. item.title: You are Scotland boss Pocognoli - what would you do?
item.description: [Getty Images] Sebastien Pocognoli's first camp in charge of Scotland ended in gloomy fashion last month as Slovenia deservedly won 2-1 at Hampden. The Belgian head coach has the chance to bounce back when his side face North Macedonia in Glasgow's southside on Friday, live on the BBC. Scott McTominay, Kieran Tierney and Che Adams are all back in the national team squad for the closing Nations League double-header, which ends with a trip to Switzerland on Monday. Put yourself in Pocognoli's shoes and pick your XI with our team selector below, while we have picked out some of the key selection dilemmas. Best set-up with McTominay return? McTominay is sure to make his first appearance under Pocognoli, but where will the Belgian deploy the Napoli star? The 29-year-old has been sitting slightly deeper in midfield for his club this season but has still managed five goals in 11 outings. Pocognoli used a 3-4-2-1 or 3-4-1-2 formation across his first four games and McTominay could well be used with John McGinn behind a central striker, given the duo's impressive strike rate at international level. Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson were the starting central midfielders in all of Pocognoli previous matches, so is that an established long-term pairing or will Ryan Christie finally get the chance to show what he can do in the area where he has excelled with Bournemouth in recent years? Of course, McTominay and McGinn are options in the middle of the pitch too. Gannon-Doak at wing-back? The width is almost certainly going to come from wing-backs despite an unconvincing beginning to Pocognoli's preferred method. Skipper Andy Robertson is a dead cert to start on the left as he closes in on the nation's caps record currently held by Sir Kenny Dalglish. Ben Gannon-Doak started the last two games on the right but the little winger is not a natural fit in the position. However, he was a dangerous attacking outlet in the 2-0 win away to North Macedonia and may be favourite to keep the jersey for an evening when Scotland are expected to have the lion's share of possession. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.description: Thu., May 26, 2022; Columbus, Ohio, USA; A person holds an Inclusive Rainbow flag as about 50 protesters gather outside the Ohio Statehouse as lawmakers debate two bills aimed at health care rights. One bill is HB 454, which would ban gender-affirming health care, such as gender reassignment surgery or the prescription of hormone blockers for people who are transgender. The other is HB 480, which would ban performing abortions. Both bills are currently in committee. Mandatory Credit: Joshua A. Bickel/Columbus Dispatch News Health Bills Protest Washington voters approved a ban on transgender girls competing in girls’ school sports in last week’s election. But the measure is already facing a legal challenge before it can even take effect. Parents of student athletes, along with the state’s teachers’ union and a trans advocacy group, have filed a lawsuit to block Initiative 638. The suit argues that the measure is discriminatory and that its sex verification requirement could subject girls to “invasive” genital examinations. Initiative 638 Initiative 638 passed with about 56% of the vote last week, even as Democrats made major gains across the country. Similar measures also passed in Arizona, Colorado, and Nebraska. The Washington measure was funded by conservative hedge fund manager Brian Heywood, and supporters argued that it protects fairness in girls’ sports. But voters in a progressive state backing it came as a surprise to many, with the Seattle Times reporting that it likely won votes from some Democrats. Critics have taken particular issue with the measure’s sex verification requirement. Girls who want to join girls’ teams must provide documentation from a medical provider confirming their sex, through hormone or genetic tests or examinations of their “reproductive anatomy,” per the Guardian . The rule does not apply to boys. The trans-athlete debate has been a hot topic since the election, with MS NOW host Rachel Maddow calling it “a fake problem.” The Lawsuit According to the Guardian’s Sam Levin , the lawsuit was filed in state court on Monday by parents of trans and cisgender girls, the advocacy group TransFamilies, and the Washington Education Association. The suit argues that the measure violates the state constitution by infringing on students’ privacy and by applying only to girls. It also argues that the ban violates a state anti-discrimination law that protects trans people. The plaintiffs include the parent of a 17-year-old trans girl who plays sports at her high school, as well as parents of two cisgender female athletes who oppose the sex verification requirement. item.description: The Green Bay Packers explored a potential trade before the NFL deadline but ultimately decided against making a move. One player on their radar was Indianapolis Colts defensive tackle Grover Stewart. item.title: Wednesday Dawg Bites Is Still Nostalgic
item.description: ATLANTA - DECEMBER 7: Tailback Musa Smith #32 of the University of Georgia Bulldogs carries the ball against the University of Arkansas Razorbacks during the SEC Championship game at the Georgia Dome on December 7, 2002 in Atlanta, Georgia. The Bulldogs defeated the Razorbacks 30-3. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Yep, this is one of those nostalgic weeks. This comes thanks to the infinite wisdom of expanding the College Football Playoff to 24 teams. That, as is well known, means that next month’s SEC Championship will now officially be the final one. For Georgia fans, playing in this event has become commonplace, but it was not always this way. In fact, until 2002, each December meant lots of watching other SEC rivals take their turn in the spotlight with Georgia fans left to wonder when that time would come..if ever. For that reason, its why when you think back to the most memorable SEC title game for Georgia, 2002 outranks them all. The whole week was a Mardi Gras for Georgia fans. Thanks to Arkansas’ enthusiasm being grossly outweighed by Georgia fans, the whole scene around the Georgia Dome was a red and black party, and the result was a foregone conclusion. Yes, there have been other sweet wins in this game for Georgia with last year’s long-awaited win against Bama and the victory a year prior against Texas. The revenge win against Auburn was satisfying, as were the separate wins against LSU, but it terms of what it meant for Georgia fans – the Arkansas win, at least from this viewpoint, will always rank at the top. In reality, the loss of the SEC title game is a microcosm of the path being driven for college football. And aren’t you glad that teams are going to be incentivized to play marquee games? About that…. The Gators have canceled their 2031-32 home-and-home series with Notre Dame, per @AP . Florida used a clause in the contract to get out without financial penalty. pic.twitter.com/vyI8elR5uI — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) November 10, 2026 Seriously. Saying this new format is great for college football is like going back to 1996 and telling long-time race fans in Wilkes County, NC that moving races away from the Carolinas to Texas and California is a long-term win the NASCAR. There was apparently some very riveting audio obtained the posting to video content from Glory Glory for their subscribers to view. But at the risk of getting a cease and desist, we won’t post it here, but it can likely be found on the backwebs. Yes, Georgia is the top-ranked team as expected in the CFP Rankings. But what does that mean to this Georgia team right now? As a south Georgia baseball coach once noted, its only good ‘for toilet paper.’ For the fourth game in a row, Peyton Woodring missed a field goal at Ole Miss. item.title: Leeds United pair join combat veterans for special Remembrance event
item.description: Leeds United pair join combat veterans for special Remembrance event Brenden Aaronson and Tarik Muharemović joined veterans to lay wreaths and observe two minutes of silence at Elland Road, before a visit to the Combat Cafe. The first team pair were special guests of a Leeds United Foundation social group that meets once a week at the stadium. "Anybody can get involved to come along and just speak to people," said Derek McHugh, a 22-year Coldstream Guards army veteran. "That's all it is. It's a group that speaks to one another, and we get support from the the club as well, especially the staff that come every week. If we need support, we can speak to them. The staff here do an amazing job, an absolutely amazing job to help us and to put this on for us every week. If we can't speak to them, we'll speak to other members of the group because we're all like-minded. We're all from the same kind of background. Even if we're army, navy, RAF, it doesn't matter. "You've got Falklands veterans here. You've got Iraq veterans. Afghanistan veterans and there's all different backgrounds from all different regiments. You've got infantry regiments, non-infantry regiments. They're all veterans but we're all here as a family." Aaronson and Muharemović were greeted in the East Stand by the veterans and along with Foundation and club staff paid tribute with a short Remembrance ceremony. "Remembrance is a massive thing for everybody," said Derek. "You might not have served, but you might have had a family member that served that you're remembering. It's great to get players down. Obviously, they wear the shirts with poppies, and it gives them a perspective of what they're wearing that poppy for, in remembrance to our fallen comrades." The group then made its way to the Gary Speed Suite for a chat about how the veterans and the players could relate their respective experiences of representing their country, working in a team and bonding as tight-knit groups. A veteran spoke of being part of something bigger than himself and discovering a brotherhood, while Aaronson agreed that making everyone feel included in a team was an important step in building something special with a team. Veterans were then able to meet the players for photos as the visit came to a close. Aaronson said: "It was amazing to hear their stories and share our experiences too. They've made this country what it is today, I have a lot of respect for veterans and people who have sacrificed their lives for their country." The free weekly sessions run exclusively for veterans and include free breakfast sandwiches and hot drinks. There are also monthly trips and activities away from the stadium, as well as regular guest speakers. There is no need to book into the drop-in sessions but for more information email fitleeds@leedsunited.com or call 0113 367 6598.
